execution_str: Signal after Close_T (frozen LIVE rule). Entry 'moo': buy at Open_(T+1), half-spread charged. Entry k: day limit buy L = Close_T x (1 - k x NATR14_T / 100) (NATR as a fraction of price), rounded DOWN to a $0.01 nominal tick. Fill on T+1: if Open <= L, at Open (marketable in the opening auction: half-spread charged); else if Low <= L x (1 - m) with m = max($0.01 / nominal Close_T, 0.1 x half-spread_T) (trade-through: a touch does not fill), at L with no spread charge; else no fill: the order expires, the slot stays empty that session, and the name can be ordered again only if its signal holds at the next close. Orders go to the top candidates by NATR up to the slots free at the decision (held names skipped, as live); unfilled orders are not backfilled intraday. Exit 'moo': today's rule. Exit 'limit': once Close_t > High_(t-1) triggers, the position is committed to exit; each following session s it rests a sell limit at Close_(s-1) rounded UP to the tick: if Open_s >= limit, filled at Open (half-spread charged); else if High_s >= limit x (1 + m_(s-1)), at the limit with no spread; else carried; after 5 unfilled sessions it sells market-on-open on the 6th (half-spread charged). A position with a resting sell keeps its slot until it fills (only a certain exit, i.e. a forced market-on-open, frees a slot at the decision). Sizing V_T / 10 / Close_T shares for every entry type. Costs: engine commissions on nominal shares ($0.005/share, $1 minimum, 1% cap); every marketable fill pays max(2.5 bp, half-spread of the session before the fill) under BOTH the per-stock Abdi-Ranaldo and the ADV-bucket pooled half-spread models (tick-floored, as the size ladder); passive fills pay commission only. The trade-through margin m uses the larger of the two half-spread models, so both cost models see the same fills. No dividends (replica convention).
expected_sign_and_location_str: Average cost per round trip falls with any limit variant (largest saving in the small-cap universes); fill rate falls as k rises; the h3 excess of filled signals is BELOW that of unfilled signals (adverse selection), more so for larger k; the net Sharpe gain over the market-on-open baseline is largest in Russell 2000 lower half and S&P SmallCap 600 and small in S&P 100 / S&P 500.
horizon_str: days (event table at h3, the P7 / size-ladder horizon; pods hold until the exit rule)
hypothesis_str: Passive limit entries below the close cut DV2's trading cost enough to make the small-cap edge net-positive; adverse selection (fills concentrate on names that keep falling) eats part of the saving.
kill_criteria_str: Hypothesis rejected if no limit variant lowers the average cost per round trip, or if no small-cap variant (Russell 2000 lower half or S&P SmallCap 600) has net Sharpe > 0 under BOTH half-spread models. A small-cap variant is a candidate only if net Sharpe > 0 under both models AND the per-asset panel MCPT (A8 null, 1000 permutations) of the whole entry x exit grid with plateau selection gives p <= 0.05. The adverse-selection part is rejected if filled signals do not have a lower h3 excess than unfilled ones.
mechanism_str: A resting limit order supplies liquidity instead of taking it, so it saves the half-spread a market-on-open order pays, and a lower limit buys the same reversal at a better price. The cost is adverse selection: a limit buy fills exactly when the name keeps falling (informed or persistent selling) and misses the names that rebound at once, which carry most of the reversal premium.

execution_str: Signal after Close_T (frozen LIVE rule; slots, NATR ranking, sizing V_T / 10 / Close_T shares and the slot rules of dv2_limit_entry_20261002 unchanged). Entry: a day limit buy for session T+1. Close anchor: L = Close_T x (1 - k x x_T), rounded DOWN to the $0.01 nominal tick; fills at Open if Open_(T+1) <= L (marketable, half-spread charged), else at L if Low_(T+1) <= L x (1 - m) (trade-through, no spread), else no fill. Open anchor: the order is placed right after the opening print, L = min(Open_(T+1) x (1 - k x x_T) rounded DOWN to the tick, Open_(T+1) - one tick); only the price uses the open, the decision (which names, how many) is made at Close_T; by construction L < Open, so it fills only by trade-through, Low_(T+1) <= L x (1 - m), at L with no spread. m = max($0.01 / nominal Close_T, 0.1 x the larger half-spread estimate at T). x_T is the offset measure, known at Close_T. For natr14, std21 and dex21_mean the multiplier k is set per universe x anchor x measure x fill target by calibration: the k whose book fill rate (entries / entry orders, limit exit) on 2004-01-01..2012-12-31 is closest to the target (bisection; the calibration book sees no bar after 2012-12-31); the same k is then run on 2004-2022. For dex63_quantile the limit is L = anchor x (1 - q_T(p)), with q_T(p) the stock's own (1 - p) quantile of its last 63 excursions (floored at 0), and the target probability p is calibrated the same way (so the comparison is at equal realized fill rate; the uncalibrated p = target is reported as a diagnostic, not a trial). Exit: the limit exit of the parent study (sell limit at the previous close, market-on-open after 5 unfilled sessions) for every entry; market-on-open exit for the best two entries on the S&P 500 (mean of AR and pooled net Sharpe). Costs: engine commissions on nominal shares ($0.005/share, $1 minimum, 1% cap); marketable fills pay max(2.5 bp, half-spread of the session before the fill) under BOTH the per-stock Abdi-Ranaldo and the ADV-bucket pooled half-spread models; passive fills pay commission only. Fill stress: the trade-through margin re-run with f = 0.1 / 0.5 / 1.0 x the larger half-spread (diagnostic). No dividends.
expected_sign_and_location_str: At the same realized fill rate, the open-anchored dex63_quantile / dex21_mean variants have higher net Sharpe under both half-spread models than close-anchored natr14 on the S&P 500, a lower round-trip cost (no marketable open fills), and filled events continue at least as well as unfilled ones after the fill day (Close_(T+1) -> Close_(T+3)); the gain replicates in S&P 100 or Russell 1000. NATR14 and std21 correlate strongly across signal-day stocks (>= 0.8); the downside excursion less so.
horizon_str: days (pods hold until the exit rule; post-fill-day continuation at Close_(T+1) -> Close_(T+3))
hypothesis_str: A limit offset scaled by the stock's own typical intraday downside excursion, anchored at the open, gives better net results than Close - k x NATR14 at the SAME fill rate.
kill_criteria_str: Hypothesis rejected if no open-anchored downside-excursion variant beats close-anchored natr14 at the same fill target on the S&P 500 under BOTH half-spread models. A variant is a candidate only if it beats the baseline on the S&P 500 under both cost models AND replicates (beats the baseline under both models) in S&P 100 or Russell 1000; then the per-asset panel MCPT (A8 null) over the registered S&P 500 grid with plateau choice must give p <= 0.05, and the paired bootstrap CI is reported (a CI that includes 0 means not shown better). A variant whose gain disappears under strict fills (f = 1.0) is not a candidate.
mechanism_str: The close-anchored limit fills partly through the overnight gap (opens below the limit pay the spread and buy names that gapped down on news); an open-anchored limit only buys an intraday dip below the open, which is the liquidity-provision event a resting order is paid for. NATR mixes up- and down-moves and overnight gaps; the downside excursion below the open measures how far a resting buy order has to wait, so at the same fill rate it should place the limit where the fill is a temporary intraday push rather than a persistent move.

execution_str: Open of the first session of month m, held to the next rebalance (alpha/scout/engines/weights). Pod = dollar-neutral: long the predicted payers (gross 1.0), short the other eligible members equal weight (gross 1.0). Costs: engine CostModel (2.5 bp, $0.005/share, $1 minimum), 25% dividend withholding on long dividends (the owner's tax case; 0% reported as a sensitivity), 1%/yr borrow on shorts, fund-scale capital $10M.
expected_sign_and_location_str: S3: date-level (one date per month) Newey-West t of the predicted payers' month-m total return minus the eligible mean is positive, about +0.2% to +0.5% a month gross, with the same sign in each of the three eras and larger for higher predicted yield. S5: active Sharpe over the equal-weight eligible members positive.
hypothesis_str: S&P 500 members predicted to go ex-dividend in calendar month m (an ex-dividend date in month m-3 or m-12) earn a higher total return over month m than the other eligible members.
kill_criteria_str: S3 hard fail (wrong sign under both estimators, or date-level t <= -2) ends the family (REJECTED). MCPT p > 0.05 or any other soft fail = WATCHLIST, no vault. Vault (opened only for a CANDIDATE, clean): net return <= T-bills over 2023-01-01..data end, or vault Sharpe below the 5th percentile of the in-sample stationary-bootstrap Sharpe for windows of the same length = FAIL, final for the family. Shadow: S8 CUSUM or Cold Blood Index red.
mechanism_str: Dividend-seeking investors (income funds, retail investors who treat dividends as free income) buy ahead of predictable payments and push prices up around the dividend month; the pressure reverses after the payment (Hartzmark and Solomon 2013).
primary_metric_str: S3 date-level Newey-West one-sided p of the month-m total-return excess (primary config m3_or_m12, EW). S5 gate: MCPT of the whole 8-config search with plateau choice, per-asset null that permutes returns and keeps the real dividend calendar fixed; score = Sharpe of the daily active return (long payers minus EW eligible); p <= 0.05. S6: T-bill slot test as a 20% sleeve of the live 60/40 book (TAA 3x 48% / NDX VXN 32% / candidate 20% vs T-bills), PASS at P >= 0.80.
schedule_str: decision at the close of the last session of month m-1, from dividends with ex-dates <= that close
source_str: Hartzmark, S. M. and Solomon, D. H. (2013), 'The dividend month premium', Journal of Financial Economics 109(3), 640-660. Scout P8 discovery, first new family (design A20).

expected_sign_and_location_str: 2x2 (VXN on/off x trend on/off): a live-change variant beats the live pod in 2000-2020 (Holm over 3) and holds in the 2021-2026 holdout.
hypothesis_str: The live NDX-VXN pod's VXN exposure scale double-counts an index trend gate (Nasdaq-100 12-month excess return > 0), so dropping one of the two, or adding the gate, would not hurt.
kill_criteria_str: Retro registration of a closed study: its verdict stands; a forward line, if any, is killed by its S8 CUSUM / Cold Blood Index.
mechanism_str: Volatility scaling and trend gates both cut exposure in bear markets; the question is whether they carry the same information.
primary_metric_str: One-sided bootstrap of the Sharpe difference vs the live pod, Holm over 3; interaction of the 2x2

Verdict: no double count; the trend gate lowers the pod's Sharpe; keep the live pod.

Large caps: limit entries cut cost per round trip about 60%, robust to strict fills; plan on S&P 500 net Sharpe about 0.70 / 0.82 at a 40% fill rate (A18). Small-cap variant not a pod. Promotion needs paper or real fill evidence (A17).
Sensitivity map (not a promotion candidate by its registration): flat ROC x filter surface; the live ROC 12 / SMA100 / top 10 sits inside the plateau; short filters hurt.

Not a promotion candidate by its registration: the E1 plateau ensemble does not narrow the luck band; the E2 ranking blend is the balanced design (later the design of record); CMMA gives no robust improvement.
No replacement for NATR20: the linear-trend ranking is the best-shaped signal (rank IC 0.023, t 1.9) but not a better strategy; it lags after 2022 (0.71).
Registered hypothesis fails: no anchor / offset variant beats Close - k x NATR14 at equal fill rate after Romano-Wolf (best adjusted p 0.13); the open anchor does not replicate (A18).
F4 passed the per-study rule, but the family-wide Romano-Wolf over all 38 filters gives adjusted p 0.19: no filter beats Close > SMA100; registered fallback, keep F0.

C passed its registered rule (luck median and 97-98% of paired draws in sample) but trailed the live pod after 2022 on 91% of draws; decision 2026-10-03: no shadow (corr 0.94, about 50 years to resolve 0.1 Sharpe); superseded by E2 as the fund design.

The 40% GICS-sector cap passed its registered rule (Max DD -24.8% -> -21.5%, Sharpe and luck median within 0.05); design of record, WIRED 2026-10-11. No S5 MCPT of its own; current GICS labels are a mild look-ahead.
Registered verdict UNCLEAR: the top-10 selection beats 200 random books (99.5th percentile) and equal weight (P 0.98), but not QQQ held at the pod's own exposure (P 0.78 < 0.80).
Report status WATCHLIST / diagnostic: the overlays fix the drawdown (-76% -> about -20%); the selection passes the in-sample rule only on 1999-2008; S5 MCPT not run.
Both registered additions dropped: the adaptive stock filter (mean P 0.26 vs the 0.80 bar) and both VIX-level gates (the VIX level is not a trend signal: -65% in the dot-com bear at VIX < 25).
Registered verdict: not a candidate. Mean P(adaptive > no filter) 0.42, P(> SPY) 0.58 (0.80 needed); the adaptive filter does not beat the SMA100 benchmark filter: a brake, not an edge.
Claimed Sharpe 1.5-2.2 not reachable from public ingredients (best 0.67 / 0.90 / 0.88).

Post-hoc pod books: B6 as extra 10% sleeve: book Sharpe 0.97, MDD -15.8% vs 0.89 / -17.6% with cash; alpha vs SPY + layer +7.5%/yr (t 2.6); post-hoc, shadow only. QS1-QS9 replications and volatility-forecast diagnostics: 4 of 9 replicated closely (QS1, QS4, QS6, QS9), 4 directionally (QS2, QS3, QS7, QS8), QS5 not reproducible (VXTLT model Sharpe 0.47 vs 0.57 VIX-only); HAR VX timing works only in 2020-04..2026-04 and loses 100% of a +-1x VX position on 2008-2020; holdout negative.

execution_str: Resting stop orders; a bar that opens beyond a level fills at its open; worst bar order is the headline and optimistic order is the other bound; exit at the stop, or at the last bar's close (P), or 15:55 market (C). expected_sign_and_location_str: Positive gross mean R on equity index ETFs, larger in high-volatility years, thin relative to costs in quiet years; the literal unfiltered ETF rule is expected to fail the house 3.5 bps frame because the stop is only 30-60 bps from entry.
hypothesis_str: A resting stop-order breakout from the regular-session open (Open +- 0.4 x ATR(5) on six ETFs; Open +- 0.25 x prior true range on NQ), stopped back at the open and flat at the close, earns a positive mean R per trade before and after costs, and reproduces the source claims (ETFs: 27% a year, Sharpe 1.04, max DD -32%, 9,023 trades, 2018 to Oct 2024; NQ: 52% CAGR, Sharpe 1.40, max DD -35%, 2018-2026).
kill_criteria_str: No kill at this round. A mean gross R that is not above zero under worst order on the literal rule ends the literal line; filters and exits are judged in later rounds on data through 2022-12-30.
mechanism_str: Intraday continuation of order-flow imbalance: short-gamma hedging by option dealers and leveraged ETF rebalancing buy after rises and sell after falls, and slow-moving capital spreads large orders across the session. A driftless random walk gives this payoff zero mean, so a positive gross mean measures intraday trending.
primary_metric_str: Replication gap against the claims (CAGR, Sharpe, max DD, trades); mean gross R per trade with a t-statistic on session sums

hypothesis_str: A two-sleeve decomposition of (1) the base Aziz/Zarattini (SSRN 5316487) eVRP + VIX/VIX3M short-vol/mid-term-vol strategy (SVXY in contango scaled by VIX/100, halved when eVRP <= 0, VIXM in backwardation when eVRP <= 0, cash when eVRP > 0 in backwardation; no RSI2 boost) and (2) an idle-cash macro trend overlay (compared across Gold-only, the 5-asset stagflation basket, and the full 13-asset non-equity pool) improves the recommended house book (TAA 50 / MR 30 / CORE5 20) at a +10% pro-rata dose with >80% bootstrap share on 2011+ even at +5 bps cost and with the 2020 COVID crash blanked.

mechanism_str: Implied volatility exceeds realized volatility on average (variance risk premium) when the VIX futures curve is in contango, while mid-term VIX futures (VIXM) provide convex crisis payoff during sustained backwardation. Because VIX-proportional sizing leaves ~74% of capital in cash on average, sweeping idle collateral into non-equity trend (primarily Gold) adds inflation/stagflation carry without margin leverage.
